Al-dharrah (the atom, or small ant): a small, red, delicate ant. It is said that it is at its smallest when a year has passed over it. Imru' al-Qays said:

"And among the wide-eyed, restrained women, if a tiny black ant crawled upon the saddle-cloth, its trace would show upon her."

It is also said that al-dharr is what is seen in the rays of the sun, the floating dust.

If it were not attributed, it would apply to every degree of earthquake, however small. ﴿because your Lord has inspired it﴾, that is, because of God's inspiration. The preposition (bi-anna) is connected to "relates". Al-Zamakhshari said: it may also mean: "On that Day it will relate with a relating that your Lord has inspired it, so that its relating of its news is because your Lord has inspired it, as when you say: 'You advised me every advice, in that you advised me in religion.'" End of quote. This is speech with a fault (ʿafash) from which the Qur'an should be exonerated. He also said: "It may be that ﴿because your Lord﴾ is a substitute for ﴿its news﴾, as if it were said: 'On that Day it will relate its news, namely that your Lord has inspired it,' because you say: 'I told him such-and-such' and 'I told him of such-and-such.'" When a verb is sometimes transitive with a preposition and sometimes transitive directly, and the preposition is not redundant, then its follower may only agree with it in case. The lam in "laha" indicates cause, meaning on account of it and because of the actions done upon it. If the inspiration is to it, it may be inspiration of inspiration (ilham), or it may be through a messenger from the angels.

﴿On that Day mankind will depart﴾. "On that Day" is governed by "will depart" (yasduru). Sadr (departing) is from a watering-place (wird). The majority said: it refers to their being buried in the earth, and sadr is their rising for the Resurrection; "ashtatan" is the plural of shatt, meaning groups: believer, disbeliever and sinner, all proceeding to the reckoning, ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾. And Allah knows best.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
